instructions.editing: Edit requests. Only enabled requests in enabled provider files run. product_guides contains copyable examples, not downloads. JSON requires double quotes and has no comments.
instructions.identity: id identifies the request; ticker is your label; input contains the provider identifier. Matching requests across providers need the same id, contract/instrument details and timeframe. Use a new id for a different instrument or period.
instructions.timeframe: Use lookback (for example 1mo or 1y) OR start (YYYY-MM-DD), plus end. end=null means today when run; otherwise end is YYYY-MM-DD. The requested range is inclusive. Returned raw responses are not clipped to this range.
instructions.metadata: Set product, operation, currency, unit, asset_class, description, exchange and frequency for the instrument. These fields describe the request; they do not convert the returned data.
instructions.raw_output: run.py saves original provider responses under tests/data_dumps. No local cleaning, resampling or price adjustment is applied; any provider-side adjustments are described below.
instructions.products: Use yield, fx or macro with operation=observations. This adapter retrieves economic series, not individual stock or option contracts.
instructions.input: input.series_id is the FRED economic-series identifier, for example DGS10. Check the series title, units, frequency and revision policy.
instructions.parameters: Use frequency=native and parameters.units=lin. Values retain the series frequency and units; yields remain observations, not bond prices.
instructions.credentials: run.py reads FRED_API_KEY from the environment. Keep the actual key outside this JSON.

observations.instructions: Use an economic-series identifier or dataset key, not a stock ticker. Set unit and frequency accurately; the provider response is authoritative.
